round_2_task: Look harder at: nil template subject (legacy), blank guard handling, .html_safe on subject downstream, other callers of CreateStageAutomationMessage

round_2_analysis.nil_subject_from_legacy_templates: When automation.channel_message_template.subject is nil (legacy templates without subject), HiringStageMessageAutomationJob passes subject: nil in message_params. CreateStageAutomationMessage calls parse_text(nil). The blank guard (return '' if text.blank?) fires because nil.blank? is true, returning ''. The channel message saves with subject: ''. In notify_candidate, @channel_message.subject.presence returns nil for '' (String#presence returns nil for empty strings), so the hardcoded fallback fires correctly. The CustomChannelMessageValidator passes because '' does not match the {{...}} regex. Full chain is correct.
round_2_analysis.html_safe_on_subject: .html_safe is retained at the end of the parse_text gsub chain, producing an ActiveSupport::SafeBuffer. The subject flows into the channel_message record and then into the Mailgun API hash as a subject: parameter in Emails::SendTemplateEmail. It is never rendered through an ERB template where html_safe would matter. The SafeBuffer behaves identically to a plain String for all non-ERB operations. The blank-guard path returns plain '' (not ''.html_safe), creating a minor type inconsistency, but this is benign since both are String subclass/instances and neither path triggers ERB rendering. No downstream issues.
round_2_analysis.other_callers: grep -rn confirms HiringStageMessageAutomationJob is the sole caller of ChannelMessages::CreateStageAutomationMessage. No other code paths need to be checked for subject propagation through this interactor.
